_about: Every number the app or a notebook reports is computed from raw logs plus this file.
Change a value and all history re-reads under the new definition; nothing is backfilled.
JSON has no comment syntax, so keys beginning with _ are documentation and the loader
Only genuine choices live here. Anything derivable from the charts is derived, anything
with one sane value is a constant in the code, and anything the set state already
determines is not restated as a policy.
Two weightings, same idea: how much of a set counts toward something it is not
entirely about. Both are switchable live in the analysis UI, and both leave the
discrete breakdown untouched — you can always ask for 6 comp sets, 2 high-spec, 3
accessory, rather than one weighted total.

muscle_roles._about: How much of a set each muscle receives. Every counting scheme people argue about is a different pair of these numbers, so there is no separate mode setting. Applies to per-muscle volume AND per-muscle stress, so the two always agree.

fractional._why: Standard in the hypertrophy literature. Ratios are contested, which is why this is switchable.

direct._why: Only what the exercise is for. The most conservative reading and the easiest to defend.

1:1._why: Every listed muscle gets a full set. Inflates totals but makes no claim about ratios at all.

tiers._about: How much of a set counts toward its base lift's event volume. A paused squat is squat work; a leg extension is squat-adjacent work; how much either counts is the question. Same mechanism as muscle roles, different axis.

graded._why: Specificity decays rather than cutting off. A sensible default for stress and for set counts.

competition._why: Only the lift and its close variations. The right lens for tonnage, where an accessory kilogram is not a competition kilogram.

flat._why: Every set counts the same. Makes no claim about specificity at all.

warmups._about: One decision, in one place, rather than repeated inside every metric. Name the metrics that count ramp-up sets.
warmups._options.counted_in: Any of: volume, tonnage, stress, records. Empty means working sets only, which is the usual reading. ['tonnage'] is the common exception — ramp-up sets are real work and some of it is heavy.

bodyweight._about: Everything about bodyweight in one place: when it is needed, how stale a hint may be, and what happens when it is missing.
bodyweight._options.hint_max_age_days: How stale a reading may be and still appear as ghost text. It is never pre-filled at any age — you always type it.

_options.when_missing.skip_set_and_warn: Excluded from load metrics and the session is flagged so you can backfill.
_options.when_missing.use_latest_known: Fall back to the most recent reading at any age. Convenient and quietly wrong.

tonnage._status: PROVISIONAL. Revisit once the analysis screens exist and it is clear what tonnage is being read for.
tonnage._options.tier_weights: Which preset from weights.tiers to apply. An accessory kilogram is not a competition kilogram, so this defaults to counting only the lift and its close variations.

_options.bodyweight_included.true: A weighted dip at 80kg bodyweight plus 20kg counts 100kg per rep.
_options.bodyweight_included.false: Only the added 20kg counts. Badly understates bodyweight work.
